task_2.title: Fix duplicate import of package __init__.py under --importmode=importlib
task_2.description: When using --importmode=importlib, package __init__.py files were imported more than once during test collection (e.g., when collecting doctests). This happened because the module name derived from the file path included a trailing '__init__' component, causing Python's import machinery to treat it as a distinct module from the package itself. The fix ensures that the module name for a package's __init__.py correctly resolves to the package name without the redundant '__init__' suffix, preventing double execution of module-level code.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when pytest is invoked with --importmode=importlib, package __init__.py files are not imported and executed more than once during test collection. Previously, collecting tests (including doctests) from packages caused __init__.py module code to run twice, which could produce side effects such as duplicated registrations, warnings, or resource allocations.

expectation.grounded: The module_name_from_path function must return a dotted module name that does not end with '__init__' for package __init__.py files. For example, a path like 'pkg/__init__.py' relative to the root must yield module name 'pkg', not 'pkg.__init__'. This ensures that the importlib-based import mechanism recognizes the module as already loaded in sys.modules and does not re-execute it.
expectation.conceptual: When pytest uses importlib-based importing, each package __init__.py should be imported exactly once during a test session, regardless of how many submodules or doctests are collected from that package. Module-level side effects in __init__.py must execute only once.

constraints.grounded: The module name computation must only strip the trailing '__init__' component; all other path components must be preserved verbatim. Regular (non-__init__) module files must continue to produce correct dotted module names. The fix must not alter behavior under the default import mode—only --importmode=importlib is affected. The module_name_from_path function must remain consistent for both packages and subpackages at any nesting depth.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not regress module name resolution for non-package modules. Import behavior under the default import mode must remain unchanged. Packages at any nesting depth must be handled correctly without double imports.

behavior: Under --importmode=importlib, the module name derived from a package __init__.py path no longer includes a trailing '__init__' segment.
Package __init__.py files are imported exactly once during test collection, even when doctests from the package are collected.
Module-level side effects (print statements, global registrations, resource initialization) in __init__.py execute only once per test session under --importmode=importlib.
sys.modules will contain a single entry for the package (e.g., 'pkg') rather than separate entries for 'pkg' and 'pkg.__init__'.
Non-__init__ modules continue to have their full dotted module name computed correctly.
acceptance_criteria: When running pytest with --importmode=importlib on a project containing a package with an __init__.py that has observable side effects (e.g., incrementing a counter or appending to a list), those side effects should occur exactly once.
When collecting doctests from a package's __init__.py under --importmode=importlib, the __init__.py module code should not be executed twice.
Given a nested package structure (e.g., parent/child/__init__.py), when running with --importmode=importlib, each __init__.py at every level should be imported exactly once.
When running pytest with --importmode=importlib on regular (non-__init__) module files, module name resolution and import behavior should remain unchanged.
When running pytest without --importmode=importlib (default mode), import behavior should remain completely unaffected by this change.

task_3.title: Preserve user_properties in JUnit XML when fixture teardown fails
task_3.description: Previously, properties recorded via record_property were lost in the JUnit XML output when a fixture's teardown also raised an error. The user_properties were only serialized during the normal test-outcome reporting path, which was bypassed or overwritten when a teardown failure produced a separate error report. The fix ensures that user_properties are always written to the JUnit XML reporter at finalization time, regardless of whether the teardown phase succeeds or fails.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that properties added via the record_property fixture are always included in the JUnit XML output for a test case, even when a fixture teardown raises an exception. Previously, if a test passed or failed and its teardown also failed, the recorded properties were missing from the resulting JUnit XML testcase element.

expectation.grounded: When LogXML finalizes a test node reporter, all entries from report.user_properties must be serialized via reporter.add_property before the reporter is finalized. This applies to every code path that calls LogXML.finalize, including paths triggered by teardown errors. The record_property fixture values must appear as <property> elements inside the corresponding <testcase> in the JUnit XML output.
expectation.conceptual: All properties recorded via record_property during a test's lifecycle must appear in the JUnit XML report for that test case. This must hold true regardless of whether the test itself passes or fails, and regardless of whether any fixture teardown raises an error.

constraints.grounded: Properties must not be duplicated in the JUnit XML output for test cases that have no teardown failures; the existing behavior for normal test passes, normal test failures, and teardown-only failures must remain unchanged. The add_property call must convert property values to strings via str() as before. The fix must not alter the behavior of xdist worker node handling or the reporter lookup/pop logic in LogXML.finalize.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not introduce duplicate properties for tests that do not experience teardown failures. Existing JUnit XML output for all other test outcomes (pass, fail without teardown error, teardown-only error) must remain unchanged. No new public API surface or configuration options should be introduced.

behavior: When a test has user_properties recorded via record_property and the test's fixture teardown raises an exception, the JUnit XML output now includes those properties on the testcase element.
When a test fails and its teardown also fails, both the failure information and the user_properties are present in the JUnit XML testcase entry.
When a test passes but its teardown fails, the user_properties are preserved in the JUnit XML testcase entry alongside the teardown error.
For tests with no teardown failures, the JUnit XML output is identical to the previous behavior — properties are still present as before.
Property values continue to be converted to strings before being written to the XML.
acceptance_criteria: When a test uses record_property to set a property and its fixture teardown raises an exception, the generated JUnit XML file must contain <property> elements with the recorded name-value pairs inside that test's <testcase>.

When a test itself raises an exception and its fixture teardown also raises an exception, the JUnit XML <testcase> must contain both the failure/error elements and the <property> elements from record_property.
When a test passes and no teardown error occurs, the JUnit XML output must include the recorded properties exactly as before (no duplication, no omission).
When a test fails and no teardown error occurs, the JUnit XML output must include the recorded properties exactly as before.
When a test passes but its teardown fails, the JUnit XML <testcase> must include both the error from teardown and the recorded properties.
Property values must be serialized as strings in the XML output, matching existing behavior.

task_1.title: Fix doctest collection for functools.cached_property decorated methods
task_1.description: Doctests embedded in methods decorated with functools.cached_property were silently skipped during collection when running pytest with --doctest-modules. The doctest finder's module-membership check did not recognize cached_property descriptors as belonging to the current module, causing their doctests to be ignored. Regular @property doctests were unaffected. The fix ensures cached_property objects are unwrapped to their underlying function before the module-membership check, restoring doctest discovery parity with regular properties. This workaround applies to Python versions below 3.13, where the upstream CPython fix is not yet available.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that doctests defined inside methods decorated with `functools.cached_property` are collected and executed when running pytest with `--doctest-modules`. Previously, these doctests were silently skipped while doctests in regular `@property` methods were collected normally, leading to undiscovered test gaps.

expectation.grounded: When the `DoctestModule` collector encounters a `functools.cached_property` descriptor on Python < 3.13, it should unwrap the descriptor to its underlying function before performing the `_from_module` module-membership check. This causes the standard `DocTestFinder` to recognize the docstring and extract runnable doctest cases from `cached_property` methods. On Python >= 3.13, the upstream CPython fix handles this natively and no override is needed. The collected doctests should appear as normal `DoctestItem` instances and execute with the same semantics as doctests from regular properties.
expectation.conceptual: Doctests in `functools.cached_property` methods should be discovered and executed identically to doctests in regular `@property` methods when using `--doctest-modules`. No doctests should be silently dropped due to the descriptor type wrapping the method.

constraints.grounded: The fix must only alter module-membership resolution for `functools.cached_property` instances and must not affect collection of doctests in regular properties, staticmethods, classmethods, or plain functions. The `_from_module` override must delegate to the parent implementation after unwrapping. On Python >= 3.13, no override should be applied since the upstream CPython fix (cpython#107995) handles this case natively.
constraints.conceptual: The change must be limited to doctest collection behavior for cached_property descriptors. It must not alter collection or execution of any other doctest sources. It must not regress doctest discovery for other descriptor types or plain functions.

behavior: When --doctest-modules encounters a class with a functools.cached_property-decorated method containing a docstring with doctest examples, those examples are now collected as test items.
On Python < 3.13, the DoctestModule's doctest finder unwraps cached_property descriptors to their underlying function before checking module membership, enabling doctest discovery.
On Python >= 3.13, no custom override is applied; the upstream CPython behavior handles cached_property doctest discovery natively.
Doctests in cached_property methods are executed with the same semantics as doctests in regular @property methods, including instance construction and attribute access in examples.
Previously silently skipped cached_property doctests now appear in test counts and can pass or fail like any other doctest.
acceptance_criteria: When a class defines a method decorated with @functools.cached_property containing doctest examples, running pytest --doctest-modules should collect and execute those doctests.
When a class has both a @property method and a @cached_property method with doctests, both sets of doctests should be collected and reported.
When a cached_property doctest contains a failing assertion, it should be reported as a test failure, not silently skipped.
When running on Python < 3.13, the cached_property unwrapping logic should be active and doctests should be collected.
When running on Python >= 3.13, cached_property doctests should still be collected via upstream CPython support without requiring the override.
Doctest collection for regular functions, @property, @staticmethod, and @classmethod decorated methods must remain unaffected by the change.

task_5.title: Improve plugin list disclaimer to clarify non-curated, non-endorsed status
task_5.description: The pytest plugin reference page automatically lists all PyPI projects matching 'pytest-*', which inadvertently included suspicious dependency-confusion placeholder packages. The previous disclaimer was minimal and did not adequately communicate that the listing is automated and not curated. The page header, description, and disclaimer were rewritten to clearly warn users that the list is not reviewed, not endorsed by the pytest project, and should not be treated as a recommendation.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the pytest plugin reference page prominently disclaims that the auto-generated plugin listing is not curated, not systematically reviewed, and does not constitute an endorsement by the pytest project or its developers. This addresses the risk of users trusting potentially malicious or placeholder packages (e.g., dependency confusion attack placeholders) simply because they appear in the official documentation.

expectation.grounded: The plugin list page generated by the update-plugin-list script should display a renamed heading ('Pytest Plugin List'), a revised introductory description clarifying the automated nature and scope of the listing, and a visible warning block. The warning must state that the list is not a curated collection, does not undergo systematic review, serves purely as an informational resource, carries no endorsement from the pytest project or its developers, and advises users to conduct their own quality assessment before adopting any listed plugin.
expectation.conceptual: The auto-generated plugin reference page should clearly communicate to users that appearing on the list does not imply quality, safety, or endorsement. Users should be warned to independently evaluate any plugin before use. The page title and description should accurately reflect the automated, non-curated nature of the listing.

constraints.grounded: The plugin list generation logic (which projects are included or excluded) must not change; only the surrounding documentation text and disclaimer are modified. The existing exclusion of inactive packages must be preserved. The warning must be rendered as a distinct, visually prominent documentation directive (e.g., a warning admonition) rather than inline prose.
constraints.conceptual: No changes to which plugins are listed or how they are discovered. The disclaimer must be prominent and unambiguous, not buried in fine print. Existing documentation structure and formatting conventions for the rest of the page must be preserved.

behavior: The plugin list page heading is updated from 'Plugin List' to 'Pytest Plugin List' to better identify the page.
The introductory paragraph is rewritten to explicitly state the list is an automated compilation of PyPI projects whose names begin with 'pytest-' plus manually selected projects.
A new warning admonition block is added below the introduction, clearly stating the list is not curated, not reviewed, and not endorsed.
The warning advises users to conduct their own quality assessment before incorporating any listed plugin.
A link to the update script is preserved for transparency about how the list is generated.
acceptance_criteria: When the plugin list documentation page is generated, the page title should read 'Pytest Plugin List'.
When a user views the plugin list page, they should see an introductory paragraph that describes the list as an automated compilation from PyPI, not a manually curated selection.
When a user views the plugin list page, a prominently rendered warning block should be visible before the plugin table, stating the list is not curated and not endorsed.
When a user reads the warning, it should explicitly advise them to conduct their own quality assessment before using any listed plugin.
When the plugin list page is generated, the link to the update script source code should remain accessible for users who want to understand the generation process.
When the plugin list page is generated, the existing filtering behavior (excluding inactive packages) should remain unchanged.

task_4.title: Fix crash when long command-line arguments are interpreted as file paths
task_4.description: Pytest crashed with an INTERNALERROR (OSError: File name too long) when users passed very long command-line arguments (e.g., lengthy comma-separated option values) because the argument resolution logic attempted to call Path.exists() on strings exceeding OS path-length limits. The fix introduces a centralized safe_exists utility in the pathlib module that catches OSError and ValueError from overly long or syntactically invalid paths, returning False instead of propagating the exception. This utility is now used consistently across collection argument resolution, conftest discovery, and directory extraction from arguments, replacing both unprotected Path.exists() calls and a previously duplicated local safe_exists helper.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest does not crash with an INTERNALERROR when a user supplies very long command-line arguments (e.g., long comma-separated values for custom options) that exceed the operating system's maximum file name length. Previously, pytest attempted to interpret such arguments as file paths and called Path.exists() without guarding against OSError or ValueError, causing an unrecoverable internal error during collection argument resolution and conftest discovery.

expectation.grounded: A centralized safe_exists utility function in the pathlib module must wrap Path.exists() and catch both ValueError (path too long on Windows) and OSError (file name too long on POSIX, or invalid path syntax on Windows), returning False in those cases. This utility must be used in resolve_collection_argument (replacing the unguarded fspath.exists() call), in PytestPluginManager's conftest anchor resolution (replacing the inline try/except for anchor.exists()), and in get_dirs_from_args (replacing the previously local safe_exists definition). When safe_exists returns False for an overly long argument, pytest must continue its normal flow (e.g., reporting 'module or package not found' or skipping conftest loading for that path) rather than raising an INTERNALERROR.
expectation.conceptual: When pytest receives a command-line argument that produces a path string exceeding OS limits, all path-existence checks must gracefully treat the path as non-existent rather than raising an unhandled exception. Pytest should continue normal execution, applying its standard error reporting for missing paths or skipping conftest loading as appropriate, instead of terminating with an internal error.

constraints.grounded: The safe_exists function must catch both ValueError and OSError to handle platform-specific failure modes (POSIX errno 36 'File name too long' and Windows invalid path syntax). Existing behavior for normal-length valid and invalid paths must remain unchanged — safe_exists must return the same boolean as Path.exists() for paths that do not trigger exceptions. The previously duplicated local safe_exists in get_dirs_from_args must be consolidated into the single pathlib-level utility to avoid drift. All call sites that previously used Path.exists() on user-supplied arguments must use safe_exists instead.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not alter pytest's behavior for normal command-line arguments and file paths. Only arguments that produce paths exceeding OS limits should be affected, and they should be treated as non-existent paths. The solution must be consistent across all platforms (POSIX and Windows) and across all code paths where user-supplied arguments are tested for path existence.

behavior: When a command-line argument produces a path exceeding the OS maximum file name length, resolve_collection_argument now returns a 'module or package not found' error message instead of crashing with an OSError INTERNALERROR.
When a conftest anchor path derived from a long argument exceeds OS limits, PytestPluginManager skips conftest loading for that anchor instead of crashing.
When get_dirs_from_args encounters an argument whose absolute path exceeds OS limits, it treats the path as non-existent and excludes it from the returned directory list.
The safe_exists utility catches both ValueError and OSError, covering POSIX 'File name too long' (errno 36) and Windows invalid path syntax errors.
For paths within normal OS limits, safe_exists behaves identically to Path.exists(), preserving all existing test discovery and collection semantics.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest is invoked with a custom option whose value is a very long string (e.g., 400+ characters of comma-separated values), pytest should not raise an INTERNALERROR and should proceed with normal test collection and execution.
When a long command-line argument is not a valid test path, pytest should report it as 'module or package not found' rather than crashing with an OSError.
When a valid test file path is specified alongside a long custom option value, the test file should be collected and run normally without any path-resolution errors.

Given a path string that triggers an OSError (file name too long) or ValueError (invalid path on Windows) when checked for existence, safe_exists should return False without propagating the exception.
Given a normal-length valid file path, safe_exists should return True, identical to Path.exists().
Given a normal-length non-existent file path, safe_exists should return False, identical to Path.exists().
Conftest discovery must not crash when processing arguments that result in overly long anchor paths — it should silently skip those anchors.
